title: Restriction of scalars preserves and reflects local derived completeness
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ any ideal sheaf. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal B$ be the ideal sheaf locally generated by images of local sections of $\mathcal J$. Use the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. An object $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],E|_U)=0$ for every object $U$ and every $f\in\mathcal J(U)$; here $\mathcal O_U$ denotes the ring sheaf on the slice site and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is sheafified sectionwise localization. Use the identical definition over $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal B$. For every $M\in D(\mathcal B)$, restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if and only if $M$ is locally derived $\mathcal J\mathcal B$-complete. No flatness or finite generation hypothesis is imposed.
